Summary: This bill would prohibit the sale, lease, rental, or offering or advertising for sale of class three e-bikes. This bill would also require retailers to disclose the speed at which a powered bicycle or powered mobility device ceases to provide assistance. A person who violates this prohibition would be liable for civil penalties up to $2,000.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring certain disclosures for sales, leases, or rentals of powered bicycles and powered mobility devices, and prohibiting the sale, lease and rental of class three bicycles with electric assist

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 20-609 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding new definitions of “class three bicycle with electric assist,” “designated citywide languages,” and “powered bicycle or powered mobility device business” in alphabetical order to read as follows: 
Class three bicycle with electric assist. The term “class three bicycle with electric assist” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision (c) of section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law. 
Designated citywide languages. The term “designated citywide languages” has the same meaning as set forth in section 23-1101.
Powered bicycle or powered mobility device business. The term “powered bicycle or powered mobility device business” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision a of section 20-610.1.
§ 2. Subdivision a of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new paragraph 3 to read as follows:
3. The speed at which such powered bicycle ceases to provide assistance is displayed on: (i) packaging of such powered bicycle; or (ii) documentation provided to the purchaser at the time of sale. 
§ 3. Subdivision b of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new paragraph 3 to read as follows:
3. The speed at which such powered mobility device ceases to provide assistance is displayed on: (i) packaging of such powered mobility device; or (ii) documentation provided to the purchaser at the time of sale. 
§ 4. Subdivision e of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 50 for the year 2024, is amended to read as follows:
e. 1. No person shall distribute, sell, lease, rent or offer for sale, lease or rental a powered bicycle, powered mobility device, or storage battery for a powered bicycle or powered mobility device online unless the required certification, [or] and the logo, wordmark, or name of such accredited testing laboratory is displayed on the online product listing page.
2. No person shall distribute, sell, lease, rent, or offer for sale, lease or rental a powered bicycle or a powered mobility device online unless the speed at which such powered bicycle or powered mobility device ceases to provide assistance is displayed on the online product listing page.
§ 5. Subdivision g of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 50 for the year 2024, is amended to read as follows:
 g.   Each failure to comply with this section with respect to any one stock keeping unit constitutes a separate violation, provided that each day that such a violation continues constitutes a separate violation.
§ 6. Subchapter 2 of chapter 4 of title 20 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 20-610.2 to read as follows: 
§ 20-610.2 Prohibition on the distribution, sale, lease, and rental of class three bicycles with electric assist. a. No person shall distribute, sell, lease, rent, or offer or advertise for sale, lease, or rental, a class three bicycle with electric assist. 
b. A person who violates this section, or any rule promulgated thereunder, is liable for a civil penalty as follows:
1. For a first violation, a civil penalty of $0; 
2. For a second violation issued on a different day than the date of a first violation, a civil penalty of not more than $1,000; and
3. For a third or subsequent violation issued on a different day than the date of a first or second violation, a civil penalty of not more than $2,000.
c. Each failure to comply with this section with respect to any 1 stock keeping unit constitutes a separate violation, provided that each day that such a violation continues constitutes a separate violation.
d. The commissioner, in consultation with the commissioner of transportation and the fire commissioner, shall conduct outreach and education in designated citywide languages to alert powered bicycle or powered mobility device businesses to the requirements of this section.
§ 7. Subdivisions a and c of section 20-762 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 51 for the year 2004, are amended to read as follows:
a. For purposes of this section, [a motorized scooter shall have the definition] the following terms have the following meanings:
Motorized scooter. The term “motorized scooter” has the same meaning as set forth in section 19–176.2 [of this code].
Stock keeping unit. The term “stock keeping unit” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-609.
c. Any person who violates subdivision b of this section shall be liable for a civil penalty of [one thousand dollars] $1,000 for a first violation and a civil penalty of [two thousand dollars] $2,000 for each subsequent violation within one year. Each [sale, lease or rental, or attempt to sell, lease or rent, a motorized scooter shall be deemed] failure to comply with this section with respect to any 1 stock keeping unit constitutes a separate violation, provided that each day that such a violation continues constitutes a separate violation. Authorized employees of the department, the police department, and of any other agency designated by the mayor, shall have the authority to enforce the provisions of this section. Such penalties shall be recovered in a civil action or in a proceeding commenced by the service of a notice of hearing that shall be returnable before the administrative tribunal of the department. In addition, such violation shall be a traffic infraction and shall be punishable in accordance with section [eighteen hundred] 1800 of the [New York state] vehicle and traffic law.
§ 8. Section 20-1526 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new subdivision d to read as follows:
d. On and before 3 years after the effective date of the local law that added this subdivision, subdivision a of this section shall not apply to a delivery service that retains, for the purpose of delivering goods on behalf of such service, a contracted delivery worker who operates a powered mobility device that is not a compliant delivery device because such device does not comply with the requirements for distribution, sale, lease, or rental pursuant to section 20-610.2.
§ 9. This local law takes effect 1 year after it becomes law.
